survey: A western saddle sits on a horizontal wooden rail, and we see it from the side. The rail runs left to right along the saddle's length and passes under the seat. The near skirt and fender are drawn in front of the rail, and the far skirt hangs behind it, showing a little to the right of the near skirt. The seat is a deep dish whose inside we see from above, with the horn on the left (its cap is a flat ellipse, so it is also seen from above) and a rounded cantle on the right. A vertical fender strap with a metal buckle comes down the near skirt and holds the near stirrup. The near stirrup faces the camera and we can see the top of its tread. The far stirrup sits a little higher and to the right, half hidden behind the near one, which fits its greater distance. The rail is one straight line on both sides of the saddle, and it is hidden in the right places (behind the near skirt, in front of the far skirt). The skirts' lower edges are level, the rail is level, and the vertical edges stay vertical.

errors.where: Wooden rail and front face of the near skirt, compared with the seat and the horn cap
errors.what: The seat dish and the horn's top ellipse are seen clearly from above, about 25–30° high. The rail is drawn almost purely as a flat front face, with only a thin hint of its top, and the near skirt is seen dead level. At that camera height the rail's top face should show as a clear band running along its full length. The rail and the saddle top look like they come from slightly different camera heights.

fix: Keep the same slightly raised three-quarter side view for the whole scene: show the top face of the wooden rail as a clear lighter band along its whole length, matching the camera height that shows the inside of the seat and the top of the horn cap; the rail stays straight and level.
